missing.what_was_said: Immediately after declaring North America and EMEA healthy, management said there was still work to do in Greater China, parts of APLA and Converse. The first-half milestone was therefore not achieved across the entire business.

Management expected to finish the Win Now actions by the end of calendar 2026. In Q&A, it specifically identified EMEA and APLA as capable of completing those actions by then, alongside the separate, longer Greater China cleanup timeline.

Management said continued supply reductions, particularly affecting NIKE Sportswear, Jordan Brand and Greater China, would pressure reported revenue through the remainder of FY2027 and into FY2028. This extended the expected revenue effects, but was not an explicit cleanup-completion deadline.

missing.what_was_said: Management increased the estimated annualized gross incremental tariff cost from approximately $1 billion to $1.5 billion, and the expected net FY2026 gross-margin headwind from approximately 75 to 120 basis points. These were changes to the headwind estimates, not a withdrawal of the full-mitigation goal.

Assuming no significant tariff changes, management expected Q1 FY2027 to be the final quarter in which higher tariffs would remain a material year-over-year gross-margin headwind. This was a year-over-year comparison forecast, not a declaration that tariff costs had been fully mitigated.

NIKE recognized a one-time $986 million benefit for recovery of IEEPA tariffs previously expensed during FY2026, but said: "Tariffs remain a dynamic cost headwind that we expect to continue looking forward." The recovery was not a declaration of full ongoing mitigation.
